newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telefonica, partners to pump $1.0 bln into CRT.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica, partners to pump $1.0 bln into CRT.

text.p: Telefonica de Espana and its new partners in Brazilian telecommunications firm Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) will jointly invest $1.0 billion in 1997 to modernize CRT, officials said.

"We are going to sit down with the government of Rio Grande do Sul state to decide a plan for the next 12 months to sort out typical problems," said Marcial Portela, president of Telefonica's overseas arm Telefonica Internacional S.A.
Those problems would include cutting waiting lists and getting new lines more quickly to customers, Portela said after a meeting with Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Telefonica joined forces with Brazilian media holding RBS Participacoes to buy a 35 percent stake in CRT in December for 681 million reais.
The state of Rio Grande do Sul has retained a 51 percent control of CRT and would participate accordingly in the investment program.
Portela expected concrete targets for modernizing CRT would be drawn up within six months.
Telefonica president Juan Villalonga said CRT would be looking for opportunities to expand into other states in Brazil's south via the upcoming privatization of the federal Telebras system.
"Our aim is to make CRT one of the most efficient Latin American telecommunications companies and to make it more efficient it has to be bigger," Villalonga said.
